editorial.headline: Plywood Manufacturing: Nationally Open, Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 16211 covers the industrial making of plywood, from ordinary panels to laminated and construction-grade sheets, but Bali blocks PMA registration for it today.
editorial.body:
KBLI 16211 is the plywood-manufacturing category: the industrial making of ordinary plywood such as tripleks, multiplex, interior plywood, and exterior plywood. Its scope also reaches construction plywood, including concrete-form plywood and waterproof plywood, which places the activity in the practical world of panels made for building, finishing, and repeated physical use. The record is broad but still specific: it is about making plywood, not trading it, designing interiors with it, or handling forestry upstream.

The category also includes laminated plywood, including laminated teak plywood, laminated rosewood plywood, polyester plywood, and decorative plywood. That matters because the code is not limited to basic sheet production. It can cover higher-finish panels where the surface treatment is part of the manufactured product. The scope extends further to plywood, including laminated plywood, made from bamboo, rattan, and similar materials. In plain English, this is a manufacturing code for turning wood or comparable plant-based material into layered panel products, from utilitarian construction sheets to decorative laminated boards.

The national picture is clear. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with a pma_max_asing of 100, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For a foreign-owned setup, that means the national classification shown here allows full foreign ownership, and the activity is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales. Those scale labels are important because the record does not reserve the activity only for large manufacturers; it shows the category open across the full listed scale range.

Bali is the hard stop. The record says l4_bali_blocked is true and gives the reason: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026.” The moratorium rule is also explicit: “Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA (island-wide, permanent).” So the honest conclusion is not that this plywood category is nationally closed; it is nationally open. The problem is local registration in Bali. A foreigner cannot register this KBLI for PMA in Bali today under the Bali-side rule recorded here.
editorial.pullQuote: This plywood category is nationally open to full foreign ownership, but Bali’s moratorium turns that national openness into a local PMA block.
